brief:
The stone-cutting workshops of the West Bank have largely fallen silent, with heavy industrial saws operating at a fraction of their former capacity due to blockades, the Palestine News Network reported. Bethlehem's quarries and cutting facilities, once mainstays of Palestinian manufacturing, now face severe operational constraints that have crippled output across the sector.

Amid the collapse of West Bank stone production, industry experts are now considering the rubble from Gaza as a potential source for reconstruction materials. The shift signals both the depth of the current crisis and emerging opportunities as reconstruction needs mount in Gaza.
dek: BETHLEHEM/West Bank In the stone-cutting workshops of the West Bank, heavy industrial saws that once hummed relentlessly now stand mostly silent, operating at barely a fraction of their capacity.
title: West Bank stone industry halts as blockades choke production
